newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Two groups mull suing over Argentine postal sale.
newsitem.headline: Two groups mull suing over Argentine postal sale.

text.p: A Brazilian-led group and an Argentine firm said Wednesday they were mulling a court challenge to an official ruling that disqualifies them from bidding for the concession to run the Argentine post.

"Our lawyers, both from Brazil and Argentina, are considering the issue," Jose Chalen, representative of the group headed by Brazilian airline VASP, told Reuters. "We will decide, probably today, the course of action to take."
Juan Bautista Ordonez, Communications Manager for Argentine building firm Roggio SA, said it was also "considering possible legal steps."

Argentina's state post office ENCOTESA said Tuesday it had rejected challenges from three groups who were disqualififed from bidding. The third group whose bid was also rejected is Dutch ING Bank NV-Cayman Islands Funds NV.

ING had said that if their challenge were rejected by the commission in charge of ENCOTESA's sale, it would go to court. But the company did not respond Wednesday to Reuters' requests for confirmation of this course of action.
Three other consortia have qualified for the concession.
The challengers had to deposit $500,000, which ENCOTESA said they would lose since their appeals failed.

Roggio and the Dutch consortium were disqualified because they did not have the backing of official post offices, while the Brazilian-led group failed to present a complete investment plan as required, ENCOTESA's President Arturo Puricelli said Tuesday. ING took Nepostel Consultancy NV as its postal operator while Roggio took Canada Post System Management Ltd (CPSM). ENCOTESA said these are not official postal operators, but consultants.
Chalen, from the Brazilian-headed group, had said it did present the investment plan, but in the body of their presentation, not separately.

The group is formed by VASP with 60 percent, local firm Brazal with 20 percent, Argentina's Banco del Chubut with 10 percent and local postal firm Andreani with 10 percent. It had proposed Italy's post office as operator.
Conditions for ENCOTESA's concession include a $250 million investment plan over the first 10 years and then on and additional annual investment of one percent over revenue.
-- Local transport company TAC, local group Roman and businessman Samuel Liberman, owner of local cable TV firm VCC, with Germany's state post office as operator.
-- Itron and Sideco --controlled by local holding company Grupo Macri-- and local Banco de Galicia, with the British Post Office.
-- Local banking group Werthein and COINTEL, a holding which controls Telefonica de Argentina, and New Zealand's Infratil International with New Zealand Post.
COINTEL is owned by halves by Telefonica de Espana, operator of Telefonica de Argentina, and Argentina's CEI Citicorp Holding SA, which is about 40 percent indirectly owned by Citicorp.
The result of the bidding will be announced July 28.
